Two half-cells are set up as follows:

Half-Cell A: Strip of Cu(s) in $CuNO_3(aq)$

Half-Cell B: Strip of Zn(s) in $Zn(NO_3)_2(aq)$

When the cells are connected according to the following diagram, the following reaction occurs. If the $Cu^+ + e^- → Cu(s)$ half reaction has a standard reduction potential of +0.52 V, what is the standard reduction potential for the $Zn^{2+} + 2e^- → Zn(s)$ half reaction?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the left half-cell is labeled with a Cu electrode, and the solution is CuNO3; the right half-cell is labeled with a Zn electrode, and the solution is Zn(NO3)2; the two sides are connected by a salt bridge labeled NaBr. The overall reaction given below the figure is 2Cu+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Cu(s) + Zn2+(aq), and it is marked E° = +1.28 V. Then reason: From the overall reaction in the figure, it can be known that Cu+ gains electrons to form Cu(s), so the copper half-reaction is a reduction reaction, and the Cu electrode is the cathode; Zn(s) loses electrons to form Zn2+, so the zinc electrode is the anode. The question gives the standard reduction potential of Cu+ + e− → Cu(s) as +0.52 V. The standard cell potential formula is E°cell = E°red(cathode) − E°red(anode). Substitute: +1.28 V = +0.52 V − E°red(Zn2+ + 2e− → Zn). Solving gives E°red(Zn) = +0.52 V − +1.28 V = −0.76 V. Note that changing the number of electrons when balancing the half-reaction does not affect the value of the standard electrode potential.

raw_record.question_text:
Two half-cells are set up as follows:

Half-Cell A: Strip of Cu(s) in $CuNO_3(aq)$

Half-Cell B: Strip of Zn(s) in $Zn(NO_3)_2(aq)$

When the cells are connected according to the following diagram, the following reaction occurs. If the $Cu^+ + e^- \rightarrow Cu(s)$ half reaction has a standard reduction potential of +0.52 V, what is the standard reduction potential for the $Zn^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Zn(s)$ half reaction?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a Cu/CuNO3 half-cell connected to a Zn/Zn(NO3)2 half-cell, with the net cell reaction and E°cell = +1.28 V printed beneath. From the image reaction, Cu+ is reduced to Cu(s), so Cu is the cathode, and Zn(s) is oxidized to Zn2+, so Zn is the anode. From the text, E°red(Cu+ + e- -> Cu) = +0.52 V. Apply E°cell = E°red(cathode) - E°red(anode): +1.28 = +0.52 - E°red(Zn2+ + 2e- -> Zn). Solve to get E°red(Zn) = -0.76 V.
